aspects.says: A new connection is in auto-commit mode, so each statement commits on its own and a failure after the first leaves it committed; a batch is no exception.
basis: section:Auto-Commit Is On, So Each Statement Commits by Itself

aspects.says: try-with-resources closes the result set and statement in reverse order, also when reading fails, and a method lent a connection leaves it open.
basis: section:A ResultSet Lives Only as Long as Its Statement

aspects.says: The generated key comes from getGeneratedKeys on the inserting statement, asked for at prepare time; SELECT MAX(id) can return another session's row.
basis: section:The Database Assigns the Key; Ask the Statement That Inserted the Row

aspects.says: getInt returns 0 for SQL NULL; wasNull() or getObject(i, Integer.class) tells NULL from 0.
basis: section:A Getter Converts; Ask getObject for the Java Type You Mean

aspects.says: A PreparedStatement is parsed once and executed with new bound values; addBatch/executeBatch sends many rows in one call into the driver instead of one call per row.
basis: section:A PreparedStatement Is Parsed Once and Bound Per Row; a Batch Sends the Rows in One Call

aspects.says: Changing the auto-commit mode during a transaction commits it, so a finally that restores the mode without a rollback commits the half-done work.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: Restoring Auto-Commit in `finally` Commits the Half

aspects.says: A ResultSet is closed when its statement is closed or executed again, so rows are read into objects before the statement closes.
basis: section:A ResultSet Lives Only as Long as Its Statement

aspects.says: getTimestamp reads a zoneless TIMESTAMP through the JVM's default zone and moves a time in a DST gap; getObject(i, LocalDateTime.class) returns the stored value.
basis: section:A Getter Converts; Ask getObject for the Java Type You Mean

aspects.says: Turning auto-commit off, committing at the end, rolling back in the catch and restoring the mode makes the statements all or nothing.
basis: section:Auto-Commit Is On, So Each Statement Commits by Itself

aspects.says: executeUpdate and executeBatch return how many rows each statement changed, and 0 means the WHERE matched nothing, not an error.
basis: section:A PreparedStatement Is Parsed Once and Bound Per Row; a Batch Sends the Rows in One Call

aspects.says: Bound values never become part of the SQL text, so the statement text is the same for every row and a value with quotes can't change it.
basis: section:A PreparedStatement Is Parsed Once and Bound Per Row; a Batch Sends the Rows in One Call
